name: AA / AAA / button batteries
why: Heavy metals leach from landfill; button cells can also be swallowed by children.
prep: Tape the terminals of button cells and 9V batteries.
Keep them in a dry tin, not loose in a bag.

name: Lithium-ion pack (phone, laptop, power bank, e-bike, vape)
why: Crushed in a garbage truck or sorting line, these ignite. US EPA counted 245 such fires at 64 waste facilities in 2013-2020 from public reports alone, and says the real number is higher.
prep: Tape the terminals, one battery per bag.
If swollen, hot or leaking: put it in sand or cat litter in a metal tin and call the site before you go.

name: Car / lead-acid battery
why: Lead and acid. Almost fully recyclable, and most dealers take them back.

name: Phones, chargers and cables
why: Contains recoverable gold, copper and cobalt, plus a battery that should never be crushed.
prep: Factory-reset and remove SIM and memory card.
Remove the battery if it comes out easily and treat it as lithium-ion.

name: Laptops, PCs and monitors
why: Lead, mercury backlights and batteries. Valuable if dismantled properly.
prep: Wipe or remove the drive first.
Take the battery out of laptops if possible.

name: Small appliances (kettle, toaster, hairdryer, fan)
why: Mostly metal and copper wire; much of it is lost when binned.
prep: Cut off long cords only if the site asks.

name: Fluorescent tubes and CFL bulbs
why: Contains mercury vapour that is released when they break in a bin or truck.
prep: Keep in the original box or wrap in newspaper.
If broken: ventilate the room, do not vacuum, pick up with tape and card.

name: Paint, solvents and varnish
why: Solvents contaminate water if poured away or landfilled.
prep: Keep lids tight, leave in the original tin.
Dry out small amounts of water-based paint with cat litter, solvent-based must go to a hazardous point.

name: Used cooking oil
why: Blocks sewers and can be turned into biodiesel.
prep: Cool it, strain it, and pour into a sealed plastic bottle.

name: Engine oil and filters
why: One litre can foul a million litres of water.
prep: Use a sealed container and never mix with other fluids.

name: Printer cartridges and toner
why: Many are remanufactured; some retailers pay or give credit.
prep: Keep in a bag so ink does not leak.
